title: Protecting Cryptographic Code Against Spectre-RSB: (and, in Fact, All Known Spectre Variants)
problem: Constant-time cryptographic code is designed to prevent timing-based secret leakage, but Spectre attacks—especially Spectre-RSB (Return Stack Buffer)—can violate constant-time guarantees by leaking secrets during speculative execution, and prior defenses cover only Spectre-v1 while leaving other Spectre variants unaddressed.
motivation: Post-quantum and classical cryptographic primitives deployed in production (e.g., Kyber) are vulnerable to the full Spectre attack surface, and a comprehensive, formally verified defense is needed to make cryptographic software provably secure against all known Spectre variants.
method: The approach has two parts: a type system that statically identifies which values depend on secrets and could leak through speculative execution channels (like the CPU cache or port contention) during any known Spectre variant including Spectre-RSB; and a compiler that rewrites low-level code to block these leaks by inserting fences (instructions that force the CPU to wait), reordering instructions, or masking values. Both the type system and compiler transformation are mathematically verified using Coq (a proof assistant) and implemented in Jasmin, a framework for high-assurance cryptographic code.
key_novelty: A Coq-verified combination of an analysis system (identifying which values depend on secrets) and code rewriter (preventing leaks during Spectre attacks) that protects all known Spectre variants (including Spectre-RSB) with below 5-7% overhead for complex cryptographic operations.
contributions: A new value-dependent information-flow type system ensuring no secrets leak under speculative execution across all known Spectre variants.
A compiler transformation for Jasmin that enforces the type-system guarantees on generated low-level code.
Coq proofs of type-system soundness and compiler-transformation correctness.
Overhead below 2% for most cryptographic primitives, 5-7% for Kyber (a complex post-quantum key-encapsulation mechanism).

metrics.other: overhead below 2% for most cryptographic primitives; 5-7% for Kyber post-quantum KEM

limitations: Protection covers all known Spectre variants but cannot guarantee safety against future undiscovered speculative execution attack classes.
primary_theme: Formally verified compiler defense against all known Spectre variants for cryptographic code
